newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends slightly lower, volume moderate.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends slightly lower, volume moderate.

text.p: COMEX copper futures ended slightly lower Tuesday on moderate volume as funds continued to take profits on the latest leg of a rally which took nearby copper to an eight-month high last week, traders said.

"Some profit taking after recent gains is healthy, but the market still remains friendly toward copper, expecting further gains of maybe $100 a tonne (about 4.0 cents a pound)," said a trade house dealer.
COMEX July copper ended off 0.05 cent at 117.10 cents a lbm, traded 117.60 to 116.15 cents.
But the contract's five-day moving average remained above its 21- and 55-day averages, analysts noted, suggesting the long uptrend remained intact.
The July/September spread ended little changed around 3.30 cents, after slipping from a high around 5.00 cents in May.
Earlier rumors China's state reserve bureau was about to sell copper provoked some nervousness, but overnight Chinese officials denied any immediate sale plans.

In North America, workers at Inco Ltd in Ontario, Canada, went on strike at the company's nickel and copper mine at Sudbury and the refinery in Port Colborne. The Ontario division produces about 90,000 tons of copper, most of which is supplied to the U.S. North East market.

"Copper prices have maintained a firm undertone due to the current tight cash (market) supply situation, expectations that a signficant global surplus may not materialize this year and continued good demand from investment funds," Smith Barney analyst, David Rinehimer said.
"The steady decline in exchange stocks highlights the current supply situation," he said.

Since the start of May, LME copper stocks have fallen from 145,750 tonnes to 132,500 tonnes Tuesday, while COMEX inventories have dropped to 42,632 short tons Monday, from 49,520 at the beginning of May.
Earlier in the year, LME copper stocks were over 200,000 tonnes, while COMEX inventories were down around 20,000 short tons.
